principles: Every visible control is rendered by @epa-wg/cem-components on the cem-elements-backed @epa-wg/custom-element substrate.
A pinned Angular Material counterpart is completed as a general CEM component before Studio composition uses missing behavior.
A reusable /studio composite may lead only when the pinned catalog has no counterpart for the composite capability.
Studio owns routes, data, selection, persistence, workers, updates, search, and command orchestration, but not control DOM or interaction semantics.

deferredGeneralCapabilities.initialBoundary: Explorer context commands remain visible cem-action or cem-icon-button controls; no popup menu is authored until the general menu container, trigger, focus, dismissal, and positioning contract is complete.
Exclusive Studio choices use cem-select until a general labeled radio-group contract is complete.
The shell uses semantic grid layout and the future completed pane switcher; it does not claim drawer, backdrop, push, or modal sidenav behavior.
Clipboard, update, and storage feedback use persistent cem-alert or status content; Studio does not invent toast duration, queue, dismissal, or focus-restoration behavior.

behaviors.requirement: One product/context header containing the current command, run state, theme choice, install/update actions, and global commands.
contractBounds: Use cem-app-bar only as its proven single title/context/action header.
Use native text/icon action variants, standalone badges, and the covered select contract; do not claim FAB, generic toolbar, or attached-badge behavior.

behaviors.requirement: Expanded explorer/editor/preview/console regions collapse to navigable panes at semantic breakpoints without losing selection.
contractBounds: cem-grid remains generic responsive layout rather than claiming Material grid-list tile semantics.
No drawer, backdrop, push mode, modal focus, or resizable-splitter behavior is claimed.
applicationOwns: preserved selected resource, run, diagnostic, and graph node

behaviors.requirement: Compact widths expose explorer, editor, preview, and console as one accessible pane switcher.
contractBounds: Use cem-tabs as the completed general local-view owner with inert cem-tab payloads, stable panels, manual activation, and no route, persistence, lazy-loading, or in-place reordering ownership.

behaviors.requirement: Recent projects, create/import, Feature Tour, storage health, offline/update status, and provider status.
contractBounds: Use cards, native actions, standalone badges, inline alerts, and the linear progress subset; no attached badge, FAB, buffer progress, or action-list contract is claimed.

behaviors.requirement: A keyboard-navigable project, subproject, data, resource, configuration, operation, and graph hierarchy.
contractBounds: cem-tree owns hierarchy, expansion, and composite focus; Studio supplies data, loading, stable selection mutation, and navigation.

behaviors.requirement: Keyboard-accessible reorder and move operations preserve stable project identities and expose recoverable results.
contractBounds: The pinned tree row deliberately excludes application data and reordering; the reusable Studio composite may coordinate stable-id moves while retaining cem-tree focus/expansion and CEM actions.

behaviors.requirement: Create, rename, copy, move, trash, restore, import, export, and run actions remain keyboard reachable.
contractBounds: Initial commands remain visible native actions. A popup menu is forbidden until the partial Material menu row gains its general container, trigger, focus, positioning, and dismissal contract.

behaviors.requirement: Search and suggestion filtering navigate project resources and commands without an app-local search widget.
contractBounds: cem-autocomplete owns editable-combobox interaction while Studio or CEM-QL owns filtering, ranking, result data, selection routing, and empty/loading outcomes.

behaviors.requirement: A source editor frame provides a native-textarea baseline, identity/revision status, source-range selection, and future adapter isolation.
contractBounds: The canonical editor is cem-textarea; the Studio frame adds document/range/revision vocabulary without implementing text editing, selection, IME, clipboard, or undo behavior itself.

behaviors.requirement: Edit explicit content type, schema, base URI, URL/snapshot, revision, and validation settings.
contractBounds: Use the proven label/help/error and choice contracts without prefix/suffix, floating-label, or projected subscript claims.

behaviors.requirement: Generate command-specific controls from the typed request schema and expose normalized configuration separately.
contractBounds: Schema interpretation and option data stay in Studio/CLI; controls retain their public value, form, validation, keyboard, and accessibility contracts. Exclusive choices use cem-select rather than an unowned radio group.

behaviors.requirement: Edit and copy a command, inspect semantic changes, select an Apply target, confirm incompatible replacement, and apply transactionally.
contractBounds: Use the passive table subset for the change preview and covered autocomplete/dialog/action contracts; command parsing and mutation remain CLI/application behavior.

behaviors.requirement: Switch among structured data, safe preview, raw bytes/text, diagnostics, report, event trace, and source trace with stable panels.
contractBounds: Use cem-tabs for the completed general tab/tabpanel interaction while Studio owns projection data, routing, and persistence; do not add app-local tab controls.

behaviors.requirement: Bounded tree/table inspection, paging, sorting, raw-source fallback, and click-to-source behavior for structured output.
contractBounds: The composite owns bounded projection/navigation vocabulary; tree hierarchy, passive table semantics, sort requests, paginator requests, and actions remain general component behavior. Studio owns data loading and row ordering.

behaviors.requirement: Group and navigate diagnostics by severity, resource, and exact source range while preserving stale/current run status.
contractBounds: The composite adds diagnostic/source-range vocabulary absent from the Material catalog; its list remains passive, badges standalone, and navigation actions native.

behaviors.requirement: Inspect reports, event traces, source maps, and graph-stage provenance as bounded navigable records.
contractBounds: Trace/provenance relationships have no Material catalog counterpart; general components retain hierarchy, table, paging, badge, and action behavior.

behaviors.requirement: Render bounded output in an isolated, non-scriptable preview while retaining metadata and safe text/download fallbacks.
contractBounds: Sandbox, CSP, byte limits, projection identity, and fallback behavior have no Material counterpart; all surrounding actions and feedback remain general CEM controls.

behaviors.requirement: Author nodes and edges, expose validation and execution state, inspect edge data, timings, provenance, and navigate to source.
contractBounds: A transformation graph and execution overlay have no Material catalog counterpart; the composite must not recreate general actions, status, hierarchy, progress, or table behavior.

behaviors.requirement: Expose queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled state, bounded progress, cancellation, and accessible status text.
contractBounds: Use determinate/indeterminate linear or circular progress, standalone badges, inline alerts, and native cancellation actions; do not claim buffer progress or attached badges.

behaviors.requirement: Explicit copy and download actions provide persistent, accessible success or failure feedback and safe fallback content.
contractBounds: Use persistent cem-alert feedback rather than inventing the partial snack-bar lifecycle; binary output is downloaded rather than guessed as text.

behaviors.requirement: Incompatible replacement, permanent deletion, migration recovery, reset, and permission changes require an accessible focused decision.
contractBounds: Use the covered native dialog lifecycle and native actions; Studio supplies the transaction, recovery, and consequence text.

behaviors.requirement: Edit defaults, resolver/network policy, budgets, storage, export, providers, and destructive settings.
contractBounds: Exclusive choices use cem-select, field composition stays within the proven label/help/error subset, and destructive operations use the covered dialog contract.

behaviors.requirement: Communicate storage durability/quota, offline snapshots, installation, update readiness, migration, and recoverable errors.
contractBounds: Use standalone status badges, linear progress, persistent alerts, native actions, and covered dialogs; no toast queue or custom install prompt is claimed.
